Regular meals arrive at her door.

needRules.note: AIC's Community Rehabilitation page names stroke, heart conditions and fractures. It suits someone who can travel; home therapy is the other option.

grantRules.name: Home Caregiving Grant
criteria: Needs some help with 3 or more of the 6 daily activities, for good
Household income of $4,800 or less a month per person
Lives at home, not in a nursing home
Singapore Citizen, or PR with a citizen parent, child or spouse
grantRules.otherConditions: Not living in a nursing home or other residential facility. Households owning more than one property get $200. Needs a Functional Assessment Report from an approved assessor, then an online application on AIC's eFASS.

grantRules.name: MediSave Care
criteria: Needs full help with 3 or more daily activities, confirmed by a severe disability assessment
A MediSave balance of $5,000 or more
Singapore Citizen or PR aged 30 or over
grantRules.otherConditions: Needs full assistance with 3 or more of the 6 daily activities, confirmed by a severe disability assessment. Withdraw from MediSave: $50 a month with a balance of $5,000 or more, up to $200 with $20,000 or more. The amount depends on the balance, not income.

grantRules.name: CareShield Life payout
criteria: Covered by CareShield Life
An MOH-accredited assessor finds she can't do 3 of the 6 daily activities
grantRules.otherConditions: For people covered by CareShield Life whom an MOH-accredited assessor finds unable to carry out 3 or more of the 6 daily activities. $689 a month is the 2026 claim amount; it is fixed by the year of the first claim.

grantRules.name: ElderFund
criteria: Singapore Citizen aged 30 or over
Needs full help with 3 or more daily activities
Household income of $1,500 or less a month per person
MediSave balance under $10,000
Not covered by CareShield Life or ElderShield
grantRules.otherConditions: For Singapore Citizens aged 30 or over who need full assistance with 3 or more of the 6 daily activities, with household income of $1,500 or less a month per person and a MediSave balance under $10,000, who aren't CareShield Life or ElderShield policyholders. Up to $250 a month. AIC considers others case by case.

grantRules.name: Helper levy concession
grantRules.amountMeaning: You pay a $60 monthly levy instead of $300.
criteria: A live-in migrant domestic worker at her address
She is a citizen aged 67 or over, or a doctor certifies she needs help with a daily activity
grantRules.otherConditions: For a household with a live-in migrant domestic worker and a Singapore Citizen aged 67 or over, or a person a doctor certifies as needing help with at least 1 daily activity.

grantRules.name: Caregivers Training Grant
grantRules.amountMeaning: $400, then $200 a year (up to $400 at a time) for approved courses.
criteria: She is a Singapore Citizen or PR aged 65 or over, or has a disability
For approved caregiver courses
Can be shared between caregivers, including a helper who is the main carer
grantRules.otherConditions: For caregivers of a Singapore Citizen or PR aged 65 or over, or with a disability, taking approved courses.

grantRules.name: Pioneer Generation Disability Assistance Scheme
grantRules.askIf: if she is a Pioneer Generation member
criteria: A Pioneer Generation member (born in 1949 or earlier, and a citizen by the end of 1986)
Permanently needs some help with 3 or more daily activities
grantRules.otherConditions: For Pioneer Generation members who permanently need some assistance with 3 or more of the 6 daily activities. Paid automatically to people already getting the Home Caregiving Grant, CareShield Life, MediSave Care or ElderFund.

alwaysBring: Your NRIC (as the person arranging care)
The hospital discharge summary or doctor's memo, if any
A list of her current medicines
A rough idea of the monthly income of everyone living at her NRIC address (subsidies are means-tested on it)

Or visit an AIC Link and they will help you apply.
Subsidies are means-tested on household income per person.

steps: Ask before she is discharged. Only the ward's medical social worker can refer her.

steps: A hospital, polyclinic or medical social worker refers her after an assessment finds she can't be cared for at home.
extraDocuments: The referral from the hospital or polyclinic

steps: A hospital, polyclinic or GP doctor refers her. An AIC Link can help with the application.
Apply about 4 weeks before. Each stay is at least 7 days, up to 30 days a year.
Call or walk in and ask what's available.
Get a Functional Assessment Report from an approved doctor, nurse or therapist.
Apply online on AIC's eFASS with Singpass.

nextSteps.label: Apply for her services
nextSteps.text: Ask her doctor at the hospital or polyclinic to apply for the services in her plan. An AIC Link can also help you apply.

nextSteps.label: Palliative care at home
nextSteps.text: Ask her doctor at the hospital, polyclinic or GP clinic to refer her for palliative care at home.
nextSteps.unlocks: Care at home for her illness, and support for the family. An AIC Link can help you apply.

nextSteps.label: Means test
nextSteps.text: Have a rough idea of the monthly income of everyone living at her NRIC address.
nextSteps.unlocks: The means test, which sets her subsidy.

nextSteps.label: Respite referral
nextSteps.text: Ask her doctor to refer her for respite care. Apply about 4 weeks before you need the break.
nextSteps.unlocks: A nursing home stay of at least 7 days, up to 30 days a year.

nextSteps.label: When your helper goes on home leave
nextSteps.text: Nursing home respite care can cover while your helper is away. A hospital, polyclinic or GP refers. Apply 4 weeks before.
nextSteps.unlocks: A short stay in a nursing home, if one has a bed free.

nextSteps.label: If the bill is still too much
nextSteps.text: Still can't pay after subsidies? Ask the medical social worker at the hospital or care provider about MediFund.
nextSteps.unlocks: Help for Singapore Citizens on subsidised care with what's left of the bill, at approved care providers.

nextSteps.label: Functional Assessment Report
nextSteps.text: Book a Functional Assessment Report with an approved doctor, nurse or therapist.
nextSteps.unlocks: Applying for the Home Caregiving Grant.

nextSteps.label: Home Caregiving Grant
nextSteps.text: Apply for the Home Caregiving Grant on AIC's eFASS with Singpass.
nextSteps.unlocks: A monthly grant, set by household income.

nextSteps.label: Severe disability assessment
nextSteps.text: Ask her doctor about a severe disability assessment by an MOH-accredited assessor.
nextSteps.unlocks: Claims for CareShield Life, MediSave Care or ElderFund.

nextSteps.label: Helper levy concession
nextSteps.text: For the helper levy concession, ask her doctor to certify the help she needs. AIC then recommends her to MOM.

nextSteps.label: Caregiver training
nextSteps.text: Pick a course in AIC's Caregivers Training Catalogue. Ask the provider to apply for the grant at least 2 weeks before.
nextSteps.unlocks: The Caregivers Training Grant pays towards the course.

nextSteps.label: Someone to talk to
nextSteps.text: If it feels like too much, call mindline on 1771 or WhatsApp 6669 1771, any time.
nextSteps.unlocks: A trained counsellor to talk to.

nextSteps.label: Other caregivers
nextSteps.text: Talk to other caregivers. Call Dementia Singapore (6377 0700), Club HEAL (6899 3463) or Mindfull Community (6460 4400).
nextSteps.unlocks: Peer support and counselling through the Caregiver Support Network.

nextSteps.label: Money for daily needs
nextSteps.text: If caregiving means you can't work, ComCare may help with daily living costs. Call 1800-777-0000, any time.
nextSteps.unlocks: Temporary support with basic living needs.

nextSteps.label: Lasting Power of Attorney
nextSteps.text: Check if she has a Lasting Power of Attorney. It names who decides for her if she loses mental capacity.
nextSteps.unlocks: Citizens can make one online with Singpass, free with Form 1. A doctor or lawyer certifies it for a fee.

nextSteps.label: Advance Care Plan
nextSteps.text: Think about an Advance Care Plan, her wishes for future care, shared with family and doctors.
nextSteps.unlocks: Find a facilitator in AIC's directory. Some community providers offer it free.

nextSteps.label: Advance Care Plan for a serious illness
nextSteps.text: With a serious illness, ask her doctor for a specially trained Advance Care Plan facilitator.

glossary.text: The means test sets her subsidy. It uses household income per person: everyone's gross monthly income, divided by the number of family members living together. With no household income, the home's Annual Value is used instead.
Subsidies are for Singapore Citizens and PRs who use services from government-funded providers.
Respite is a short break from caregiving, while someone else cares for her. It can be at home, in a day centre, or in a nursing home. A nursing home stay is at least 7 days, and up to 30 days a year.
It shows how much help she needs with daily activities. A GP, or an approved doctor, nurse, physiotherapist or occupational therapist, does the assessment. There may be a fee.
Washing, dressing, feeding, using the toilet, moving around indoors, and moving between bed and chair. CareShield Life and ElderShield pay out when she can't do 3 or more of them.
